category: Style keys: edges, containers and behaviour
description: Style keys that shape connectors (routing, arrowheads, terminal points, animation), that turn a vertex into a container with automatic child layout, that embed images and indicators, and that constrain what the user may do with a cell (move, resize, rotate, connect, edit). Together with the shape/fill/text keys these cover the vocabulary needed to generate or parse any draw.io style string.

tools.name: elbow (style key)
tools.description: For edgeStyle=elbowEdgeStyle chooses whether the single bend is horizontal (default: horizontal segment first) or vertical. The Format panel's Waypoints dropdown writes Simple (elbow horizontal) and Simple Vertical. The companion key segment=<px> sets the length of the first straight segment for elbow and segment styles.

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.description: Leave the source horizontally, bend once (default).

parameters.name: vertical
parameters.description: Leave the source vertically, bend once.

parameters.name: segment
parameters.description: Length in px of the first segment (elbowEdgeStyle / segmentEdgeStyle).

tools.notes: Dragging the elbow handle adds a single waypoint that fixes the bend position. Use orthogonalEdgeStyle when more than one bend may be needed.

tools.name: curved (style key)
tools.description: Draws the edge as a smooth curve through its waypoints instead of straight segments; with orthogonalEdgeStyle this yields rounded S-curves, with no edge style a Bezier through the waypoints. It is the Curved option in the Format panel Waypoints dropdown and is common for mind maps and sequence flows.

parameters.description: Curved rendering.
Straight segments (default).

tools.notes: Mutually exclusive in effect with rounded=1 (curved wins). Curved edges cannot show line jumps.

tools.name: orthogonalLoop (style key)
tools.description: Makes self-loops (source == target) and edges between overlapping cells route orthogonally with jettySize offsets instead of the default round loop. draw.io's default edge style includes orthogonalLoop=1 together with jettySize=auto so that connectors leaving and re-entering the same shape look consistent.

parameters.description: Orthogonal loop routing.
Classic loop (loopEdgeStyle) rendering.

tools.notes: Only affects edges whose two terminals are the same cell or overlap.

tools.name: jumpStyle (style key)
tools.description: Draws line jumps where this edge crosses other edges, so crossings are distinguishable from junctions. Values are none (default), arc, gap and sharp; the Format panel calls it Line jumps and jumpSize sets the jump width in pixels. Jumps are computed per edge, so enable the key on the edges that should hop.

parameters.name: arc
parameters.description: Semicircular hop.

parameters.name: gap
parameters.description: Break in the line.

parameters.name: sharp
parameters.description: Triangular hop.

parameters.name: jumpSize
parameters.description: Jump width in px, default 6.

tools.notes: Not rendered on curved edges. Line jumps are included in SVG/PNG export.

tools.name: jumpSize (style key)
tools.description: Width in pixels of the line jump drawn where an edge with jumpStyle crosses another edge. Larger values make crossings more obvious on thick lines; the default is 6.

parameters.name: jumpSize
parameters.description: Pixel width of the hop, default 6.

tools.notes: Has no effect unless jumpStyle is arc, gap or sharp.

tools.name: endArrow / startArrow (style keys)
tools.description: Arrowhead drawn at the target (endArrow) and source (startArrow) end of an edge. Values include classic (default for endArrow), classicThin, block, blockThin, open, openThin, oval, diamond, diamondThin, dash, cross, circlePlus, circle, halfCircle, async, doubleBlock, box, baseDash, the ER notation set ERone, ERmandOne, ERmany, ERoneToMany, ERzeroToOne, ERzeroToMany, and none. The Format panel's Line start / Line end dropdowns write these keys.

parameters.name: classic / classicThin / block / blockThin / open / openThin
parameters.description: Standard arrowheads; *Thin variants use a narrower angle.

parameters.name: oval / circle / circlePlus / halfCircle / diamond / diamondThin / box
parameters.description: Symbol markers (UML aggregation uses diamond, composition diamond with endFill=1).

parameters.name: dash / cross / async / doubleBlock / baseDash
parameters.description: Line markers used by UML and BPMN.

parameters.name: ERone / ERmandOne / ERmany / ERoneToMany / ERzeroToOne / ERzeroToMany
parameters.description: Crow's-foot cardinality markers for entity-relationship diagrams.

parameters.name: none
parameters.description: No arrowhead.

tools.notes: Whether a marker is filled is controlled by endFill/startFill; size by endSize/startSize. UML generalisation is endArrow=block;endFill=0.

tools.name: endFill / startFill (style keys)
tools.description: Whether the end/start arrowhead is filled with strokeColor (1) or hollow (0). Hollow markers express UML inheritance (block, endFill=0), aggregation (diamond, endFill=0) versus composition (diamond, endFill=1), and oval/circle ports. The Format panel toggles this through the filled/unfilled variants in the arrow dropdown.

parameters.description: Filled marker (default for classic and block).
Outline only.

tools.notes: Ignored by markers that have no interior (open, dash, cross).

tools.name: endSize / startSize (style keys)
tools.description: Size in pixels of the end/start arrowhead (default 6, scaled by strokeWidth). On swimlanes and containers startSize has a second meaning: the height (or width when horizontal=0) of the header band. The Format panel exposes arrow sizes next to the Line start/end dropdowns.

parameters.name: endSize
parameters.description: Target arrowhead size, default 6.

parameters.name: startSize
parameters.description: Source arrowhead size, or swimlane header size (default 23 for swimlanes).

tools.notes: For ER markers endSize controls the crow's-foot width.

tools.name: exitX, exitY, entryX, entryY (style keys)
tools.description: Fix the point where the edge leaves the source (exitX/exitY) and enters the target (entryX/entryY) as fractions of the terminal's bounds: 0,0 is top-left, 0.5,0 top-centre, 1,1 bottom-right. Dropping an edge end onto one of a shape's blue connection points writes these keys; without them the router picks the nearest side dynamically.

parameters.name: exitX / exitY
parameters.description: Relative source point.

parameters.name: entryX / entryY
parameters.description: Relative target point.

tools.notes: Values may exceed 0..1 to attach outside the bounds. exitPerimeter/entryPerimeter=0 keeps the exact point instead of projecting it onto the perimeter; exitDx/exitDy add pixel offsets.

tools.name: exitDx, exitDy, entryDx, entryDy, exitPerimeter, entryPerimeter (style keys)
tools.description: Refine fixed terminal points: exitDx/exitDy and entryDx/entryDy add absolute pixel offsets to the relative exitX/exitY and entryX/entryY point, and exitPerimeter/entryPerimeter=0 stops the point from being projected back onto the shape perimeter (default 1). draw.io writes all of them when an edge is snapped to a connection point so the attachment survives resizing.

parameters.name: exitDx / exitDy
parameters.description: Offset of the source point in px.

parameters.name: entryDx / entryDy
parameters.description: Offset of the target point in px.

parameters.name: exitPerimeter / entryPerimeter
parameters.description: 1 projects the point onto the perimeter (default), 0 uses it as-is.

tools.notes: Connection points declared on a shape via points=[[x,y,perimeter,dx,dy],...] carry the same five values.

tools.name: sourcePerimeterSpacing / targetPerimeterSpacing (style keys)
tools.description: Gap in pixels between the edge end and the source/target shape perimeter, set on the edge rather than on the vertex (compare perimeterSpacing). Use it to keep arrowheads clear of a border or to leave room for a port symbol.

parameters.name: sourcePerimeterSpacing
parameters.description: Gap at the source end, default 0.

parameters.name: targetPerimeterSpacing
parameters.description: Gap at the target end, default 0.

tools.notes: Ignored when the end is attached to a fixed connection point with exitPerimeter/entryPerimeter=0.

tools.name: portConstraint, sourcePortConstraint, targetPortConstraint (style keys)
tools.description: Restrict the sides through which edges may leave or enter a shape. portConstraint on a vertex accepts north, south, east, west or combinations (e.g. eastwest); sourcePortConstraint/targetPortConstraint on an edge restrict one end only. portConstraintRotation=1 makes the constraint rotate with the shape.

parameters.name: portConstraint
parameters.description: Allowed sides on a vertex, e.g. eastwest or northsouth.

parameters.name: sourcePortConstraint / targetPortConstraint
parameters.description: Allowed side at the edge's source/target.

parameters.name: portConstraintRotation
parameters.description: 1 rotates the constraint with the cell's rotation.

tools.notes: The orthogonal router honours the constraint; fixed connection points override it.

tools.name: points (style key)
tools.description: Declares the fixed connection points a shape offers (the blue crosses shown when hovering with an edge). Each entry is [x, y] in relative coordinates, optionally [x, y, perimeter, dx, dy]. points=[] removes all connection points, which draw.io uses on edge labels and text. The Edit Connection Points dialog (Edit > Edit Connection Points, Alt+Shift+Q) edits this key interactively.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: Relative position 0..1 in the cell bounds.

parameters.name: perimeter
parameters.description: Optional 0/1: project onto the perimeter.

parameters.name: dx, dy
parameters.description: Optional pixel offsets.

tools.notes: Stencils define their own points through <connections>; a points= key on the cell replaces them.

tools.name: jettySize, sourceJettySize, targetJettySize (style keys)
tools.description: Length of the short straight stub an orthogonal or elbow edge keeps perpendicular to the terminal before turning. jettySize=auto (draw.io default) derives it from the terminal size; a number fixes it in pixels and sourceJettySize/targetJettySize set each end individually. Increase it when edges should exit further from a shape before bending.

parameters.name: jettySize
parameters.description: auto or px for both ends.

parameters.name: sourceJettySize / targetJettySize
parameters.description: Per-end override in px.

tools.notes: Applies to orthogonalEdgeStyle, elbowEdgeStyle and segmentEdgeStyle only.

tools.name: noEdgeStyle (style key)
tools.description: Forces straight-line rendering for an edge even if a default edgeStyle is inherited from the diagram's default edge style or a containing stylesheet entry. The Format panel writes noEdgeStyle=1 when Waypoints is set to Straight; the inverse (removing the key) restores routing.

parameters.description: Ignore any edgeStyle; draw straight segments through the waypoints.

tools.notes: Distinct from omitting edgeStyle, because default styles (configuration key defaultEdgeStyle) may inject one.

tools.name: flowAnimation (style key)
tools.description: Animates the edge's dash pattern so the line appears to flow from source to target, useful in lightbox/HTML embeds to show data or process flow. flowAnimation=1 is written by the Format panel's Flow Animation checkbox; flowAnimationDirection=normal|reverse and flowAnimationTimingFunction (CSS timing keyword) tune it. Animation is rendered with CSS/SMIL in the browser and in SVG export.

parameters.name: flowAnimation
parameters.description: 1 enables the animation.

parameters.name: flowAnimationDirection
parameters.description: normal (source to target) or reverse.

parameters.name: flowAnimationTimingFunction
parameters.description: CSS animation-timing-function value.

tools.notes: Static PNG/PDF exports show the first frame. The custom-link action 'flow' toggles this key at run time, and the 'flow' plugin adds a context-menu toggle.

tools.name: Edge shapes (shape=connector, link, flexArrow, arrow)
tools.description: Edges also accept a shape key: connector (default single line), link (double parallel lines, as in the Link entry of the sidebar), flexArrow (thick outlined arrow with adjustable width, the 'Bidirectional/thick arrow' connectors) and arrow (the mxGraph solid block arrow). flexArrow reads width (shaft width), endWidth/startWidth and endSize/startSize for the head geometry.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: Two parallel strokes; fillColor fills the space between them.

parameters.name: flexArrow
parameters.description: Outlined arrow; keys width, endWidth, startWidth, endSize, startSize, fillColor.

parameters.name: arrow
parameters.description: Classic thick arrow edge shape.

tools.notes: flexArrow and arrow ignore the ordinary arrowhead keys except endSize/startSize. Edge shapes still honour edgeStyle for routing.

tools.name: container (style key)
tools.description: Marks a vertex as a container: shapes dropped onto it become its children, move with it and are clipped to it in exports. Groups, swimlanes, pools, AWS/Azure group boxes and tables are containers; the Format panel Arrange tab's Container checkbox writes this key. Combine with collapsible=1 for a fold button and with childLayout for automatic arrangement.

parameters.description: Accept drops; children are stored under this cell's id as parent.
Not a drop target (default for plain shapes).

tools.notes: In the XML, children have parent="<container id>" and geometries relative to the container origin. dropTarget=0 blocks drops on a container without removing existing children.

tools.name: collapsible (style key)
tools.description: Shows the small minus/plus fold button on a container so it can be collapsed to its header (collapsed="1" in the mxCell, with alternateBounds in mxGeometry storing the other size). collapsible=0 hides the button on swimlanes and groups that should never fold; the Format panel Arrange tab exposes it as Collapsible.

parameters.description: Fold button visible (default for swimlanes).
No fold button.

tools.notes: Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End collapse and expand the selection; the viewer parameter nav=1 keeps folding available in lightbox mode. The configuration key defaultFoldingEnabled disables folding globally.

tools.name: childLayout (style key)
tools.description: Applies an automatic layout to the children of a container every time they change: stackLayout (vertical or horizontal stack, used by lists and UML classes), treeLayout, flowLayout (hierarchical), circleLayout, organicLayout and tableLayout (tables). Stack containers additionally read horizontalStack, stackFill, stackBorder, stackUnitSize, marginLeft/Right/Top/Bottom, resizeParent, resizeParentMax and resizeLast.

parameters.name: stackLayout
parameters.description: Children stacked; horizontalStack=1 for a row.

parameters.name: treeLayout
parameters.description: Compact tree of the children (treeFolding/treeMoving apply).

parameters.name: flowLayout
parameters.description: Hierarchical (layered) layout.

parameters.name: circleLayout / organicLayout
parameters.description: Circle or force-directed layout of the children.

parameters.name: tableLayout
parameters.description: Row/column layout used by shape=table.

tools.notes: Arrange > Layout runs a layout once; childLayout keeps re-running it. The Insert > Layout menu entries for containers write these keys.

tools.name: stackFill, horizontalStack, stackBorder, stackUnitSize (style keys)
tools.description: Tuning keys of childLayout=stackLayout: horizontalStack=1 arranges children left-to-right instead of top-to-bottom; stackFill=1 stretches each child to the container's width (or height); stackBorder=<px> is the inner border; stackUnitSize=<px> snaps child sizes to a unit. The sidebar's List, UML class and Kanban/columns shapes are built from these.

parameters.name: horizontalStack
parameters.description: 1 = row, 0 = column (default).

parameters.name: stackFill
parameters.description: 1 stretches children across the stack.

parameters.name: stackBorder
parameters.description: Padding inside the container in px.

parameters.name: stackUnitSize
parameters.description: Size grid for children in px.

tools.notes: Children of a stack are usually given movable=0 or part=1 so they cannot be dragged out of order (reordering happens by drag within the stack).

tools.name: resizeParent, resizeParentMax, resizeLast, resizeLastRow (style keys)
tools.description: Control how a stack/table container reacts to its children: resizeParent=1 grows and shrinks the container to fit; resizeParentMax=1 only grows it; resizeLast=1 stretches the last child to fill leftover space; resizeLastRow=1 does the same for the last row of a table. They are read by the child layouts and by table editing.

parameters.name: resizeParent
parameters.description: Fit container to children.

parameters.name: resizeParentMax
parameters.description: Container may only grow.

parameters.name: resizeLast
parameters.description: Last child absorbs remaining space.

parameters.name: resizeLastRow
parameters.description: Table: last row absorbs remaining height.

tools.notes: recursiveResize=0 on a plain group prevents children from scaling when the group is resized, which is a different mechanism.

tools.name: marginLeft, marginRight, marginTop, marginBottom (style keys)
tools.description: Inner margins in pixels applied by childLayout=stackLayout between the container border (below the header) and the stacked children. UML class shapes set marginBottom=0 so the last compartment touches the border; list shapes use small symmetric margins.

parameters.name: marginLeft / marginRight
parameters.description: Horizontal inset of children.

parameters.name: marginTop / marginBottom
parameters.description: Vertical inset (top is measured below the swimlane header).

tools.notes: Only stack layouts read these keys; use spacing* keys for label padding.

tools.name: startSize, swimlaneLine, swimlaneFillColor (swimlane style keys)
tools.description: Keys specific to shape=swimlane (pools, lanes, UML classes, lists): startSize is the header height (or width when horizontal=0), swimlaneLine=0 removes the line between header and body, swimlaneFillColor colours the body separately from the header's fillColor, and separatorColor tints the separator. horizontal=0 turns the header into a vertical band on the left.

parameters.name: startSize
parameters.description: Header size in px (default 23).

parameters.name: swimlaneLine
parameters.description: 0 hides the header separator.

parameters.name: swimlaneFillColor
parameters.description: Body fill; default none (transparent).

parameters.name: horizontal
parameters.description: 0 rotates the header to the left side with vertical text.

tools.notes: swimlaneHead=0 and swimlaneBody=0 (used by some templates) hide the header or body outline. Lanes inside a pool are nested swimlanes with childLayout=stackLayout on the pool.

tools.name: treeFolding / treeMoving (style keys)
tools.description: Behaviours for tree-shaped diagrams (org charts, mind maps): treeFolding=1 shows a fold button that hides the whole subtree reachable through outgoing edges, and treeMoving=1 makes dragging a node move its descendants along. Both are written by the Tree templates and by Arrange > Layout > Vertical/Horizontal Tree on containers.

parameters.name: treeFolding
parameters.description: 1 enables subtree collapse from a node.

parameters.name: treeMoving
parameters.description: 1 moves the subtree with the node.

tools.notes: The 'trees' plugin adds keyboard tree editing on top of these keys. Folding state is kept in the cell's collapsed attribute.

tools.name: movable, resizable, rotatable, deletable (style keys)
tools.description: Per-cell permissions checked by the editor: setting any of them to 0 removes the corresponding handle or action. They are exposed as checkboxes in the Format panel Arrange tab (Property section) and are all set to 0 together with editable=0, connectable=0 and locked=1 by Edit > Lock/Unlock (Ctrl+L).

parameters.name: movable
parameters.description: 0 pins the cell in place.

parameters.name: resizable
parameters.description: 0 hides resize handles; resizeWidth/resizeHeight=0 restrict one axis.

parameters.name: rotatable
parameters.description: 0 hides the rotation handle.

parameters.name: deletable
parameters.description: 0 makes Delete a no-op for the cell.

tools.notes: Select All still selects such cells; locked=1 additionally removes them from selection unless Edit > Unlock is used.

tools.name: editable, connectable, cloneable, bendable, locked (style keys)
tools.description: More per-cell permissions: editable=0 blocks label editing and Edit Data, connectable=0 stops edges from attaching (used on table cells and edge labels), cloneable=0 prevents Ctrl+drag/duplicate, bendable=0 removes waypoint handles from an edge, and locked=1 is the flag written by Lock/Unlock that makes the cell unselectable until unlocked.

parameters.name: editable
parameters.description: 0 disables in-place editing and metadata edits.

parameters.name: connectable
parameters.description: 0 hides connection points and rejects edge terminals.

parameters.name: cloneable
parameters.description: 0 disables cloning/duplication.

parameters.name: bendable
parameters.description: 0 fixes the edge's waypoints.

parameters.name: locked
parameters.description: 1 marks the cell as locked (Ctrl+L).

tools.notes: Locked cells are skipped by rubber-band selection and Select All; Edit > Select > Locked? is not available, so use Edit > Unlock on the layer or Edit Diagram to change them.

tools.name: allowArrows (style key)
tools.description: allowArrows=0 hides the four blue hover arrows (clone-and-connect) on a specific shape while keeping it connectable, which is useful for background boxes and images that are frequently hovered. View > Connection Arrows (Alt+Shift+A) toggles the arrows globally instead.

parameters.description: Suppress hover arrows on this cell.
Show them (default).

tools.notes: The configuration key defaultConnectionArrowsEnabled sets the global default.

tools.name: pointerEvents (style key)
tools.description: Whether the transparent interior of an unfilled shape (fillColor=none) reacts to the mouse. pointerEvents=0 lets clicks pass through to shapes underneath, so a large hollow frame does not block selecting what it encloses; pointerEvents=1 (default) makes the whole area clickable.

parameters.description: Interior is click-through.
Interior captures clicks (default).

tools.notes: Only relevant for shapes without fill; filled shapes always capture events. Alt+Click selects the cell below the pointer regardless.

tools.name: autosize, resizeWidth, resizeHeight (style keys)
tools.description: autosize=1 makes the vertex grow to fit its label after every edit (the Arrange tab's Autosize checkbox; Ctrl+Shift+Y applies it once). resizeWidth=1 / resizeHeight=1 limit the automatic resize to one axis, and resizable=0 with resizeWidth=1 gives a shape that only grows horizontally. Text shapes from the sidebar set autosize=1 by default.

parameters.name: autosize
parameters.description: 1 re-fits the cell to its label after editing.

parameters.name: resizeWidth / resizeHeight
parameters.description: Allow automatic resize on that axis only.

tools.notes: Autosize uses the current fontSize and whiteSpace; with whiteSpace=wrap only the height grows.

tools.name: metaEdit (style key)
tools.description: metaEdit=1 makes double-click open the Edit Data dialog instead of the in-place label editor, for shapes whose visible label is generated from placeholders or whose data matters more than the text. It is written by the 'Edit data on double-click' style used by data-driven templates.

parameters.description: Double-click opens Edit Data (Ctrl+M).
Double-click edits the label (default).

tools.notes: Placeholders are enabled by the placeholders=1 attribute on the wrapping <object>, not by a style key.

tools.name: image (style key)
tools.description: URL or data URI of a raster/SVG image rendered inside the cell. With shape=image the picture is the whole shape; with the label shape (shape=label) the image sits beside the text; any other shape draws it as an icon. Arrange > Insert > Image and drag-and-drop of image files write this key, embedding small files as data:image/...;base64 URIs so the diagram stays self-contained.

parameters.name: image
parameters.description: Absolute URL, path relative to the app (img/lib/...), or data URI.

parameters.name: imageAspect
parameters.description: 0 stretches the image to the cell; 1 preserves its ratio (default).

tools.notes: External URLs need CORS headers for PNG export (draw.io proxies them through its server unless offline). The configuration keys maxImageSize and maxImageBytes cap embedded images.

tools.name: imageAlign, imageVerticalAlign, imageWidth, imageHeight, imageBackground, imageBorder (style keys)
tools.description: Position and decorate the image inside a shape=label cell: imageAlign=left|center|right and imageVerticalAlign=top|middle|bottom place it, imageWidth/imageHeight fix its size in px, imageBackground fills behind it and imageBorder draws a border around it. The sidebar's 'Label with image' and list-item shapes use these keys.

parameters.name: imageAlign / imageVerticalAlign
parameters.description: Placement of the image inside the cell.

parameters.name: imageWidth / imageHeight
parameters.description: Image size in px (default 24).

parameters.name: imageBackground / imageBorder
parameters.description: Colours behind and around the image.

tools.notes: For shape=image (picture only) these keys are ignored except imageAspect.

tools.name: indicatorShape, indicatorColor, indicatorWidth, indicatorHeight, indicatorImage (style keys)
tools.description: Draw a small indicator glyph (a secondary shape or image) inside a label cell, typically at the left of the text, to flag status or type. indicatorShape names any vertex shape (ellipse, rhombus, triangle, ...), indicatorColor/indicatorStrokeColor/indicatorGradientColor colour it, indicatorWidth/indicatorHeight size it, indicatorSpacing sets the gap to the label and indicatorImage substitutes a picture.

parameters.name: indicatorShape
parameters.description: Shape name drawn as the indicator.

parameters.name: indicatorColor / indicatorStrokeColor / indicatorGradientColor
parameters.description: Indicator colours.

parameters.name: indicatorWidth / indicatorHeight / indicatorSpacing
parameters.description: Geometry in px.

parameters.name: indicatorImage
parameters.description: Image URL used instead of a shape.

tools.notes: Indicators only render for the label shape (shape=label) and its derivatives.

tools.name: backgroundOutline (style key)
tools.description: For 3D-looking stencils such as cylinder3, cube and some AWS/Azure containers, backgroundOutline=1 draws the outline of the background part so that hidden edges appear when the fill is transparent or the shape is placed over others. The sidebar sets it on cylinders and process shapes by default.

parameters.description: Outline the background element of the stencil.
Do not (default for most shapes).

tools.notes: boundedLbl=1 in the same styles keeps the label inside the drawable part of the stencil.

tools.name: enumerate / enumerateValue (style keys)
tools.description: enumerate=1 overlays a small numbered badge on each cell that carries the key, numbering them in model order; this is the Enumerate checkbox in the Format panel Property section and is handy for step-by-step process diagrams. enumerateValue=<text> replaces the automatic number with a fixed string.

parameters.name: enumerate
parameters.description: 1 shows the badge.

parameters.name: enumerateValue
parameters.description: Custom badge text instead of the running number.

tools.notes: The 'number' plugin adds a similar numbering overlay across the whole diagram without editing styles. Badges are included in exports.

tools.name: part (style key)
tools.description: part=1 marks a child cell as an integral part of its parent: it is selected and moved together with the parent, cannot be dragged out, and is skipped by layouts. Composite sidebar shapes (a box with separately styled ports or labels, table cells, list items) use it so users interact with the whole rather than the pieces.
tools.usage: part=1;   (on a child of a group/container)

parameters.description: Treat as a part of the parent.

tools.example: <mxCell id="port1" style="ellipse;fillColor=#000000;part=1;connectable=1;" vertex="1" parent="box"><mxGeometry x="-6" y="20" width="12" height="12" as="geometry"/></mxCell>
tools.notes: Parts remain individually connectable unless connectable=0. Alt+click selects a part directly.

tools.name: dropTarget / recursiveResize (style keys)
tools.description: dropTarget=0 prevents other cells from being dropped into a container (it keeps existing children), which is useful for decorative frames that must not swallow shapes. recursiveResize=0 stops a group's children from being scaled when the group is resized, so the group behaves like a fixed frame around free-floating children.

parameters.name: dropTarget
parameters.description: 0 rejects drops even when container=1.

parameters.name: recursiveResize
parameters.description: 0 leaves children untouched when the parent is resized (default 1 scales them).

tools.example: group;container=1;recursiveResize=0;dropTarget=0;   (frame that neither scales nor accepts drops)
tools.notes: The Format panel exposes both under Property when a group or container is selected.

tools.name: shape=table, tableRow and partialRectangle (table style keys)
tools.description: Tables are containers with shape=table;childLayout=tableLayout whose rows are shape=tableRow and whose cells are shape=partialRectangle with connectable=0 and overflow=hidden. Cell borders are controlled by the partialRectangle keys top/left/bottom/right (0 hides that side), merged cells carry colspan/rowspan, and rowLines=0 / columnLines=0 on the table hide interior lines. Arrange > Insert > Table generates this structure and the table toolbar edits it.

parameters.name: childLayout=tableLayout
parameters.description: Row/column layout engine on the table container.

parameters.name: top/left/bottom/right
parameters.description: 0/1 per side of a partialRectangle cell.

parameters.name: colspan / rowspan
parameters.description: Merged-cell spans.

parameters.name: rowLines / columnLines
parameters.description: 0 hides interior lines of the table.

parameters.name: fixedRows / resizeLastRow
parameters.description: Row height behaviour when the table is resized.

tools.example:
<mxCell id="t" value="" style="shape=table;startSize=0;container=1;collapsible=0;childLayout=tableLayout;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="40" y="40" width="180" height="80" as="geometry"/></mxCell>
<mxCell id="r1" style="shape=tableRow;horizontal=0;startSize=0;swimlaneHead=0;swimlaneBody=0;top=0;left=0;bottom=0;right=0;collapsible=0;dropTarget=0;fillColor=none;points=[[0,0.5],[1,0.5]];portConstraint=eastwest;" vertex="1" parent="t"><mxGeometry width="180" height="40" as="geometry"/></mxCell>
<mxCell id="c11" value="A1" style="shape=partialRectangle;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;connectable=0;overflow=hidden;fillColor=none;top=0;left=0;bottom=0;right=0;" vertex="1" parent="r1"><mxGeometry width="90" height="40" as="geometry"/></mxCell>
tools.notes: Cross-functional flowchart templates are tables whose first row/column are headers (shape=tableRow with swimlane heads). Arrange > Insert > Advanced > From Text with the Table type builds a table from tab-separated text.

tools.name: stencilFlipH / stencilFlipV (style keys)
tools.description: Flip only the stencil drawing of a custom or library shape (not the label or child cells) horizontally or vertically. Use them when flipH/flipV would also mirror attached text or when a stencil's own handles must stay put; the electrical and P&ID libraries expose them for mirrored components.

parameters.name: stencilFlipH
parameters.description: 1 mirrors the stencil graphics left-right.
